/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 16 June 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2670 (-50)
Baltic Capesize Index: 3911 (-142)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2266 (-25)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1685 (21)
Baltic Handysize Index: 910 (5)
CAPESIZE
The market endured another difficult session, with the BCI 182 5TC shedding a further $1,285 to close at $35,471. In the Pacific, the presence of all three major C5 miners supported a more active trading environment, although rates struggled to build sustained momentum. C5 remained relatively flat overall, easing marginally by $0.050 to $10.710. Bids were initially reported in the very low $10s, before a series of fixtures, estimated at 8–10, were concluded around $10.60-$10.70 levels. In contrast, the Atlantic basin came under increased pressure, with sentiment weakening throughout the session. The C3 index suffered a sharp decline of $1.900 to $32.609 as sentiment deteriorated further. A significant gap has emerged between charterers and owners, with bids reported around $30 and offers closer to $34 for mid-July dates, resulting in limited activity. North Atlantic sentiment was also reported softer.
PANAMAX
Market sources today pointed to a clear divergence in market sentiment between the Atlantic and Pacific basins. Brokers described the Atlantic as relatively active, with a steady flow of fresh mineral and grain enquiry across both the trans Atlantic and fronthaul routes, broadly balanced against available tonnage. Some owners are said to have shown willingness to fix at levels close to recently concluded levels, preferring shorter duration employment in an attempt to keep their tonnage trading within the Atlantic. Conversely, the Pacific market continues to face pressure, with sources pointing to a lack of cargo and a growing build-up of prompt tonnage, weighing on rates and overall confidence. Demand from East Coast Australia and the North Pacific remains subdued, while Indonesia is comparatively more active, particularly for slightly forward dates. The P5TC dropped today by $224 to $20,393 primarily reflecting the ongoing weakness in the Pacific market.

Asia
Cargill were reported to have covered their North Pacific to China requirement with petcoke but further details lacked. The RB Lisa (81,364 2016) open Yosu 19/20 June was said to have been placed on subjects, but again further details were unknown. The Shandong Xin Xing (82,138 2024) was reported as fixing for an East Coast Australia round at $21,000 + $195,000 ballast bonus to Richland with arrival dates unclear.
SUPRAMAX
An indifferent day with patchy information although Atlantic rates are said to remain bullish, whilst in Asia the market at least appears to be flat and trending sideways despite very few reported trades.
The BSI rose to 1,685, whilst the 11TC average gained another $265 to close at $21,304. The US Gulf saw the biggest improvements in the Indices again today, but it was talk of Ultramax’s fixing from the East Mediterranean for fronthauls via EC South America that captured the most attention. The SSI Phoenix (63,734 2024) open Nemrut Bay supposedly agreed $24,500 for the trip via EC South America to Asia and the Akmi (63,689 2020) open Egyptian Mediterranean was rumoured at $25,000 (basis scrubber benefit for Charterers) for the same route, but there were no further details on either trade.
HANDYSIZE
It was a generally quiet day for the sector across both basins, with limited fresh activity emerging. The BHSI climbed to 910, while the 7TC average rose by $96 to close at $16,385. Across the Continent and Mediterranean, only marginal changes were observed, with rates quoted slightly firmer than previous levels. A 34,000-dwt vessel open on the Continent was fixed for a trip delivery Skaw via the Baltic to West Africa at $15,000, although further details were not disclosed. Meanwhile, the South Atlantic and US Gulf continued to gain momentum, with market sources highlighting the firming rates despite limited reported fixtures and little fresh information. In Asia, conditions remained largely unchanged, with the market appearing well balanced and no notable shifts in sentiment or activity. A 35,000-dwt vessel open Indonesia on 19/26 June was heard fixed for a trip via Australia to China at $15,000, although further details were not disclosed. Additionally, a Handysize vessel was rumoured fixed from China to West Coast India at $25,000, while a small Handysize was heard fixed via East Coast India to Vietnam with steels in the $12,000s, though further details were lacking.

Market Fundamentals
China Crude Steel Production

Chinese crude steel production declined 2.7% on the year to a four-month low of 84.4 Mt in May, bringing Jan-May output 3.9% below to 415.5 Mt, National Bureau of Statistics data show. Meanwhile, Chinese blast furnace capacity utilisation averaged at around 90% in May, a 0.4 percentage-point increase from the prior month, with daily molten iron output near flat on the month at 2.4 Mt/day in May, MySteel data show. Around 63.4% of the 247 sampled mills were in profit on average in May, a 14.5 percentage-point rise from the prior month and the highest share so far this year.

Trading Commentary
Cape
A volatile day in the Cape FFA market with resistance across the curve during the morning session, resulting in 28000 being sold on Jul, 29350 Aug and 29700 Q3. Despite the index losing $1285 which was lower than expect, the market began to rally higher with pays on the Jul up to 29250, 30500 on Aug and 30700 Q3. The Q4 was stable throughout the day, trading marginally lower on open down to 31600 then back up to 32250. There was limited activity on the Q1 with prints between 22750-23150, while the Cal27 made significant gains trading up 27000. The Cal28 went through in huge volume today between 23050 and 23300.

PMX
The pmx market traded actively today. The session opened with steady selling interest across the curve finding support into the close. Jun traded lower from 20,500 to 20,250 before recovering somewhat late in the day to 20,450 . Jul traded actively from the outset, with repeated prints around 20,200-20,250. Aug and Sep followed a similar pattern, trading mostly lower through the morning and recovering into the close. Q3 traded heavily between 19,800 - 20,100 early on, finishing the day around 20,750, Q4 traded down to 18,800 before finding support recovering to 19,600. Cal 27 improved to 15,750.

SMX + HANDY
Mixed trading to start the day in the SMX market, as July help relatively flat to previous day’s close

ai_analysis.summary: BDI下跌50点至2670，Capesize大幅走弱（BCI跌142点，C3跌$1.900至$32.609），但Supramax逆势上扬（BSI涨21点至1685），Panamax呈大西洋与太平洋分化格局，整体干散货市场情绪偏空，CapesizeAtlantic端压力尤为明显。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: Capesize引领跌势，C3/C8/C14航线全线下滑，大西洋端下行压力显著。Panamax出现大西洋与太平洋分化，大西洋相对活跃而太平洋承压。Supramax成为唯一亮点，11TC升至$21,304，所有航线上涨。Handysize稳中有升，7TC报$16,385。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: Capesize期货近月趋弱（Jun $34,825跌$，Q3 $30,625跌$425），但Cal27反弹至$27,050显底部支撑。Supramax期货全面上扬（Jun $21,163，Q3 $21,638），市场看涨情绪浓。Panamax期货近月小幅上扬后回落，远期曲线趋平。FFA市场显示CapesizeBackwardation结构强化。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: AtlanticCapesize空头信号明确，C3与C8大幅下跌， charterer出价与owner要价差距扩大至$4。Supramax大西洋航线强势可持续（S1C_63 $31,979，S4A_63 $32,593），建议关注其与Capesize的价差机会。Panamax大西洋端可逢低布局，太平洋端暂观望。

market_watch: C3航线Capesize大幅下跌$1.900，Atlantic端情绪走弱，注意charterer与owner价差风险
Supramax 11TC升至$21,304，大西洋航线全面走强，可关注短期上行空间
Panamax P1A大西洋端报价$17,200-$19,355，活跃度尚可但上行承压

route_focus.view: C3跌$1.900至$32.609，Atlantic端情绪恶化，charterer出价$30与owner要价$34差距显著，短期内仍有下行压力，期货市场Backwardation结构支持空头逻辑。
Transatlantic RV报价$17,200-$19,355，大西洋端相对活跃但broker提示货盘有限，短期内区间震荡为主，缺乏明确方向。
Skaw-Passero至Rio航线$7,193，小幅上涨$64，Handysize大西洋航线稳中有升，运价处于历史低位但基本面支撑有限。
